title: Proper finite coefficient extension in intrinsic coordinates
statement:
For a proper map of Noetherian schemes and finite commutative coefficient rings A to B, the canonical intrinsic direct-image scalar mate is invertible on an ordinary etale origin J whenever J and its actual coefficient extension are bounded below. The functors are the specified canonical ones of [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison], [lem-exc-etale-origin-proper-open-interchange] and [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor].

theorem properIntrinsicFiniteCoefficientExtension
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (φ : A →+* B) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f]
    (J : Etale.DerivedCategoryModule (ULift.{u + 1, u} A) X)
    (_hJ : ∃ n : ℤ, J.IsGE n)
    (_hBJ : ∃ n : ℤ,
      ((Etale.scalarExtension (RingHom.ulift.{u + 1, u + 1, u, u} φ) X).obj J).IsGE n) :
    IsIso ((directImageScalarComparison φ f).app
      ((etaleOriginOpenComparison A X).obj J))

source.place: Tag 0GL6, proper case; site comparison Tag 09A6

proof.text: Form the normalized intrinsic site/direct-image comparison as the ambient canonical site mate followed by the inverse direct-image presentation. Its components at J and its actual scalar extension are isomorphisms by the two lower bounds and bounded-below qcqs comparison. Proper maps are qcqs.

Apply the existing properFiniteCoefficientExtension to the lifted finite coefficient map and J. The etale coefficient mate is invertible. Rewrite the intrinsic coefficient/site square by intrinsicCoefficientSiteMate; every factor on the etale side is invertible. Cancel the invertible scalar image of the A-site mate and the invertible direct image of the scalar presentation to conclude that the intrinsic coefficient mate is invertible.
